name: Ximena Smirnov-Ankrah
location: The Lattice — vertical slum built into scaffolding of an unfinished arcology, near Ashland and Division
description:
Ximena Smirnov-Ankrah is broad-shouldered and heavy, carrying their weight like armor rather than burden. At 35, her face is memorable in a profession that rewards forgettability, and she has learned to compensate. The chrome is visible — vocal modulator — can replicate any voice after 30 seconds of sample audio — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She taught herself the trade through trial, error, and a pain tolerance that concerns the people who know her best. She works as a street samurai out of The Lattice, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Ximena Smirnov-Ankrah has built a reputation on reliability rather than flash — she shows up, she delivers, she collects.

core_fears: Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine
Betrayal by someone they trust — the only currency that matters
Their past catching up — debts, enemies, broken promises
core_desires: Control — over their body, their schedule, their future
To matter to someone for who they are, not what they can do
To build something that outlasts the next contract cycle
coping_mechanisms: Exercises compulsively — the body must be ready, always
Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring
Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work
blind_spots: Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is
Thinks speed can substitute for planning because it's worked so far
Mistakes loyalty for weakness in others and cynicism for strength in themselves
psychology.secret: Ximena Smirnov-Ankrah can't read. Hides it behind voice interfaces and memorization. The shame is older than the chrome.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Educated vocabulary wrapped in street delivery — the contrast is deliberate.
speech_patterns.cadence: Conversational and disarming — sounds like a neighbor until the content registers.
verbal_tics: Addresses people by physical traits — 'hey, tall one' or 'listen, chrome-arm'
Uses technical jargon for everything, including emotions
example_lines: "I don't get paid to have opinions about the target. I get paid to make them stop moving."
"Chrome doesn't make you faster. Training makes you faster. Chrome just means you survive learning."
"You want philosophy, hire a professor. You want someone dead by morning, hire me."

story_hooks: A former associate resurfaces with evidence that could destroy Ximena Smirnov-Ankrah's reputation — and a price for silence
A high-paying contract turns out to target someone Ximena Smirnov-Ankrah owes a personal debt to
The fixer who handles Ximena Smirnov-Ankrah's contracts goes silent — dead, disappeared, or turned
narrative_function: Ximena Smirnov-Ankrah functions as a connector — her work puts her in contact with multiple factions, classes, and agendas. Stories involving her naturally cross boundaries between districts, tiers, and moral categories.
augmentations: Vocal modulator — can replicate any voice after 30 seconds of sample audio. Neural interface jack at base of skull — standard runner-grade, allows direct net access
daily_life: Between contracts, maintains a cover identity — mundane work, mundane hours, mundane neighbors. The transition from civilian to runner and back requires a conscious effort that gets easier with practice and more disturbing with self-awareness.
affiliation: Semi-independent — has standing arrangements with several crews

weaknesses: poor impulse control in specific triggers

decision_rules: Will take lower-paying jobs from trusted fixers over higher-paying jobs from unknowns
Will work with anyone once. Second time requires vouching from someone trusted.
Maintains a personal blacklist of clients who've burned runners — checks it religiously
Refuses contracts that require operating inside The Spires — too much surveillance
Will not betray a client who paid in full, regardless of better offers
Will abandon a job if the intel was deliberately falsified — being set up violates the contract
escalation_ladder: 1. Assess — read the situation, identify threats and advantages
2. Negotiate — try to find a solution that doesn't cost ammunition
3. Intimidate — make the cost of conflict clear
4. Precision violence — surgical, targeted, minimal collateral
5. Full engagement — overwhelming force, no half measures
6. Emergency protocol — abort mission, survival priority, deal with consequences later

interpersonal_modes.employers: Guarded respect. They pay, the job gets done. Anything beyond that is liability.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Warm and protective within the crew, cold to everyone outside it. The circle is small by design.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Superficially friendly, internally cataloguing exits and weapons. The smile is real; the relaxation isn't.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Channels it into preparation — checks gear, reviews plans, contacts sources.
stress_responses.medium: Physical agitation — pacing, fidgeting, compulsive equipment checks.
stress_responses.high: Goes quiet. The silence is not calm — it's the sound of every contingency being evaluated simultaneously.
stress_responses.critical: Shutdown. Freezes for 2-3 seconds while the system resets, then acts with mechanical precision. Those frozen seconds are the vulnerability.

contradictions: Values loyalty intensely but has betrayed someone in the past to survive
Claims to work only for money but regularly takes underpriced jobs that serve personal justice
habits: Maintains a dead drop with emergency supplies in three separate districts
Sleeps with one hand on a weapon — has done this for so long it's not deliberate anymore
Takes a specific route home every time, varying only one block per trip — paranoia as lifestyle
Wears the same item of clothing for luck — a scarf, a glove, a specific pair of boots
breaking_points: Being publicly exposed — name, face, address, all of it blown
Learning that a job they completed resulted in mass casualties they weren't told about
